paths.description: Homepage and live-score dashboard, the primary entry surface; tested on desktop/mobile and under dark, reduced-motion and increased-contrast preferences.
Live match commentary and score detail, representing the highest-value real-time task.
News article detail, representing editorial content and share/discovery metadata; tested on desktop and mobile.
International schedule listing, representing dense date/time and listing content.
Account sign-in entry, representing the primary form and authentication surface; no credentials or CAPTCHA completion attempted.
Deliberately invalid route used to assess HTTP/content recovery guidance and useful onward navigation.

findings.summary: The site does not honour the user’s dark theme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark/reduced/contrast capture remains the same light rgb(236, 240, 241) surface with black text as the light capture; computed color-scheme is normal and inspected CSS has no prefers-color-scheme rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and provide preference-driven dark tokens with light-dark() or prefers-color-scheme.

findings.summary: High-contrast preferences are not explicitly supported and existing contrast failures remain.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-contrast: more the CSS probe found no prefers-contrast or forced-colors rules; Lighthouse reports 3.92:1 for GET APP and lower ratios in consent controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors and prefers-contrast adaptations, and raise all essential text/control contrast to WCAG minimums.

findings.summary: Route and state changes do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection across representative pages found no view-transition declarations; navigation uses ordinary links and abrupt document/state replacement.
findings.suggestedFix: Add progressive cross-document or same-document View Transitions to high-frequency navigation and tab changes, with reduced-motion fallbacks.

findings.summary: Navigation chrome does not react to scroll state.
findings.evidence: Desktop captures show a static header and the CSS probe found no scroll-state container queries or scroll-driven progress treatment across a long 8,636px homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Use scroll-state queries or a lightweight sticky-header treatment to preserve context without consuming excess space.

findings.summary: Dropdown/menu positioning does not use anchor positioning.
findings.evidence: The site exposes several dropdown navigation menus, while CSS inspection found no anchor-name, position-anchor, or fallback position rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Use CSS anchor positioning with position-try fallbacks for menus and contextual overlays.

findings.summary: A full-screen consent interruption obscures all content on first load.
findings.evidence: The initial 1440x1000 screenshot is dimmed behind a centered consent dialog; users must choose before reading scores or news. Reject is available and visually equal, which limits severity.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep consent legally compliant but minimise its footprint, retain an immediate equal reject option, and avoid blocking non-personalised core content where policy allows.

findings.summary: Transient UI relies on custom role-based markup instead of native overlay primitives.
findings.evidence: The CMP is a div with role=dialog rather than <dialog>; across inspected pages there are zero dialog, popover, or details elements despite menus and disclosures.
findings.suggestedFix: Use native dialog/popover/details primitives for authored overlays and disclosures, preserving third-party CMP accessibility requirements.

findings.summary: Advertising and app-promotion chrome competes heavily with cricket content.
findings.evidence: Mobile first viewports contain an install banner, top ad, in-feed video ad, GET APP promo, and fixed bottom navigation; the HAR records 81 third-party requests before the core page settles.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce ad density above and within primary content, defer recommendation units, and reserve the first viewport for scores/articles and essential navigation.

findings.summary: Responsive layouts are viewport-driven rather than component-driven.
findings.evidence: Desktop/mobile layouts do adapt, but inspected CSS across reused cards contains no @container rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce size container queries for reused score, video, and article cards so they respond to their available space.

findings.summary: Some controls have weak focus treatment or undersized targets.
findings.evidence: The focused logo link reports outline none; structured probes found 12–30 visible controls below 24px on representative pages, and Lighthouse flags 56x14px sponsored controls on the article.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a strong :focus-visible style and ensure every independent target has at least 24x24 CSS pixels of safe clickable area, preferably 44x44 for primary touch controls.

findings.summary: Lab Core Web Vitals miss the good range on primary pages.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports homepage LCP 3.4s, CLS 0.155, TBT 300ms and article LCP 2.7s, CLS 0.22, TBT 340ms; performance scores are 0.68 and 0.69.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP element, reserve all dynamic slots, and delay third-party execution until after core content becomes interactive.

findings.summary: Late content causes visible cumulative layout shift, especially on mobile article pages.
findings.evidence: The layout observer measured CLS 0.110 on the mobile homepage and 0.191 on the mobile article; Lighthouse measured 0.155 and 0.22 respectively.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve stable dimensions for ad/CMP/app-promo slots and images, and prevent late modules from displacing read content.

findings.summary: Third-party work delays interactivity despite a clean short trace window.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measures 300–340ms TBT and 18.9–19.7s Time to Interactive; the custom post-load trace saw no long tasks, indicating the main cost is concentrated during load.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer and chunk non-critical scripts, use priority-aware scheduling, and keep advertising/analytics off the critical interaction path.

findings.summary: The critical load has a long, third-party-heavy dependency surface.
findings.evidence: HAR captured 140 requests and 2,218,614 transferred bytes, including 69 scripts; 81 third-party requests transferred 1,627,042 bytes. Parser-inserted stylesheets and high-priority script chains start at navigation.
findings.suggestedFix: Shorten critical dependency chains, self-host/trim critical fonts, defer ad technology, and apply useful cache policies to remaining resources.

findings.summary: Large amounts of shipped JavaScript and CSS are unused on initial load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 769 KiB unused JavaScript and 36 KiB unused CSS; top waste includes Taboola, GPT, GTM, CleverTap, and k-words scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Conditionally load monetisation and analytics integrations, remove overlapping tags, and split page code by actual feature use.

findings.summary: Important links and the email input lack accessible names/labels.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse finds the logo and carousel links have no discernible name; login inspection finds an email input with no label, aria-label, id/name, required state, or autocomplete.
findings.suggestedFix: Give icon links explicit accessible names and pair every input with a visible <label>; expose required state programmatically.

findings.summary: Text and controls fail WCAG contrast minimums.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports 3.92:1 for 14px GET APP controls and lower ratios in consent UI; article ad attribution also measures about 4.14:1 at small text sizes.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust green, grey, and overlay tokens so normal text reaches 4.5:1 and large/essential UI reaches the applicable WCAG threshold.

findings.summary: Heading order and keyboard focus are inconsistent.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse flags an H3 Featured Videos heading that skips hierarchy on the homepage; the first logo link is focusable but computed outline is none.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a logical heading hierarchy and apply a consistent, high-contrast :focus-visible ring to every interactive element.

findings.summary: The viewport prevents user zoom.
findings.evidence: Every inspected page uses maximum-scale=1.0 and user-scalable=no; Lighthouse fails meta-viewport and also flags small article targets. Layout otherwise reflows without horizontal overflow at 360px.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove maximum-scale and user-scalable=no; retain width=device-width and allow browser zoom. Increase small target spacing.

findings.summary: Advertising integrations emit console/network errors on load.
findings.evidence: The homepage probe captured CORS failure for Amazon APS and HTTP 400 from prebid-server; Lighthouse independently fails errors-in-console.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix or remove failing auction endpoints and isolate third-party failures so routine page loads are clean.

findings.summary: Some image assets are not proportionately sized.
findings.evidence: Document doctype and UTF-8 charset are valid, but the image audit found one image missing dimensions and eight 400–640px team images rendered at only 24px.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve correctly dimensioned responsive variants and keep explicit intrinsic width/height on every image.

findings.summary: Deprecated and inspector issues remain in third-party code.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports deprecated Topics API use from sdk.k-words.io, cookie inspector issues, and a BFCache eviction caused by an advertising frame redirect.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove deprecated integrations, resolve cookie warnings, and ensure third-party frames do not block BFCache where controllable.

findings.summary: The default robots policy blocks all unspecified crawlers.
findings.evidence: robots.txt says User-agent: * followed by Disallow: /, while only named crawlers such as Googlebot receive exceptions. The site is public and has a current sitemap, so generic and many AI/search crawlers cannot crawl it.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the blanket default block with explicit sensitive-path exclusions, preserving intentional controls for unwanted bots.

findings.summary: Security headers and cookie attributes are incomplete.
findings.evidence: HTTPS, HSTS, nosniff, and SAMEORIGIN are present, but CSP is missing; all 11 observed first-party cookies lack Secure and many use SameSite=None, including long-lived analytics/ad identifiers.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive CSP and set Secure plus appropriate SameSite attributes on all cookies; keep sensitive cookies HttpOnly.

findings.summary: The default page has an unusually broad tracking footprint.
findings.evidence: Tracker capture found 31 third-party origins and 12 known tracker domains; HAR shows 81 third-party requests transferring 1.63 MB, including Taboola, DoubleClick, GTM, Criteo, CleverTap, Amazon Ads, and ScorecardResearch.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimise vendors, gate non-essential tags on consent, batch necessary analytics, and document a strict data-purpose budget.

findings.summary: Several browser-enforced defensive policies are missing.
findings.evidence: Headers inspection found no CSP, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy; HSTS max-age is only 86400 seconds. Clickjacking and nosniff protections are present.
findings.suggestedFix: Add CSP with frame-ancestors, strict Referrer-Policy, a least-privilege Permissions-Policy, and a longer HSTS policy after deployment validation.

findings.summary: Dates and times are not adapted to the visitor locale.
findings.evidence: The server identified the visitor as GB, but the schedule and article render US-style JUL 23 and “Tue, Jul 21, 2026 • 6:10 PM” with no locale control or locale-specific formatting signal.
findings.suggestedFix: Format dates, numbers, and times through Intl using the user’s chosen locale, with a visible locale preference where audience needs justify it.

findings.summary: Match and publication times lack explicit time-zone context.
findings.evidence: The schedule displays dates/times for a global audience without a timezone label or user-zone affordance; the article timestamp similarly gives 6:10 PM without a zone.
findings.suggestedFix: Store instants unambiguously and render the viewer’s time zone with an explicit zone or conversion affordance.

findings.summary: The sign-in form hides requirements behind a disabled action.
findings.evidence: The email, agreement, and CAPTCHA controls are not programmatically required; Continue is disabled with no inline explanation or aria-live error state, and the blank-state probe found no :invalid or role=alert feedback.
findings.suggestedFix: Mark required fields semantically, explain unmet requirements next to the disabled action, and announce validation after interaction.

findings.summary: The sign-in email field does not support autofill semantics.
findings.evidence: The email field is type=text and has empty autocomplete, name and id values, with only “Email Id” as a placeholder.
findings.suggestedFix: Use type=email, autocomplete=email, a stable name/id, and a persistent visible label.

findings.summary: Small icons are sourced from much larger images.
findings.evidence: Image audit found eight team images naturally 400–640px wide but displayed at 24px; although the image CDN often negotiates WebP, source URLs request 0x0 originals.
findings.suggestedFix: Request size-appropriate CDN variants and responsive sources instead of full-size originals for 24px icons.

findings.summary: Large background advertising and analytics stacks run during the initial experience.
findings.evidence: 69 script requests transfer 1.53 MB, while Lighthouse estimates 769 KiB unused JS and TTI near 19 seconds; several auction/tracking calls also fail.
findings.suggestedFix: Delay non-essential background work until consent and idle time, remove duplicate vendors, and stop failed/redundant auction calls.

findings.summary: Third parties dominate the page’s network budget.
findings.evidence: Third parties account for 81 of 140 requests and 1,627,042 of 2,218,614 transferred bytes (73%); the largest scripts are Taboola, DoubleClick, GTM, CleverTap, and ad bidders.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/request budget, defer below-fold recommendations, and enforce vendor performance/resource contracts.

findings.summary: The homepage has a heavy steady-state DOM/listener footprint for a content surface.
findings.evidence: Performance metrics show about 10,474 DOM nodes, 1,713 event listeners and 28.2 MB JS heap used after consent rejection; the heap snapshot contains 617,337 V8 nodes and 36.3 MB self size.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce third-party widgets and repeated DOM, virtualise long recommendation feeds, and release listeners for off-screen modules.
